status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 the structural changes in this objective have been made by the 2025 reconciliation law (Public Law 119-21, signed 2025-07-04) and ED's implementing final rule, Reimagining and Improving Student Education (91 FR 23768, published 2026-05-01, effective 2026-07-01). The Congressional Research Service describes the law's changes: Grad PLUS is eliminated for periods of instruction beginning on or after 2026-07-01 (Sec. 81001), graduate unsubsidized loans are capped at $20,500 a year and $100,000 in total, professional loans at $50,000 a year and $200,000 in total, and Parent PLUS loans remain but are limited to $20,000 a year and $65,000 per dependent undergraduate. A new Repayment Assistance Plan (Sec. 82001) sets payments at 1 to 10 percent of total adjusted gross income, with the rate rising one point for each $10,000 of income above $10,000, less $50 a month per dependent and with a $10 monthly minimum, cancels remaining balances after 30 years, and, with a tiered standard plan of 10 to 25 years, becomes the main option for new borrowers; existing income-driven plans stay available to existing borrowers through 2028-06-30, and income-contingent repayment is repealed on 2028-07-01. The final rule implements these provisions. A federal court in D.C. set aside the rule's extra requirements for defining professional degrees on 2026-06-24, and other challenges are pending. This differs from the Mandate's design in that Parent PLUS is limited rather than eliminated, payments are a graduated share of total income with no poverty-line exemption rather than 10 percent of income above the poverty line, and balances are canceled after 30 years.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is signed; per the Congressional Research Service its higher education provisions end Grad PLUS for new periods of instruction from 2026-07-01 (Sec. 81001), set graduate, professional and Parent PLUS limits, and create the Repayment Assistance Plan and a tiered standard plan while phasing out other income-driven plans (Sec. 82001).

ED publishes its final rule implementing the loan provisions of Public Law 119-21 (91 FR 23768, effective 2026-07-01, following a proposed rule published 2026-01-30 that drew 80,793 comments): new loan limits, the end of Grad PLUS for new borrowers, the Repayment Assistance Plan, a tiered standard plan, and the end of income-contingent repayment after 2028-07-01. Thompson Coburn reports the rule's professional-degree definition added requirements beyond the statute.
Twenty-six states file Maryland v. ED (D. Md.) seeking professional-degree status for programs such as audiology, physician assistant, and physical therapy.

D.D.C. in American Association of Nurse Practitioners v. McMahon (consolidated) sets aside and stays the rule's extra-statutory requirements; the government did not appeal, and ED must apply the statute's three-part test.

Statutory annual and aggregate caps take effect for loans made after this date: graduate $20,500 and $100,000, professional $50,000 and $200,000; Parent PLUS is capped at $20,000 a year and $65,000 per dependent undergraduate, and the Repayment Assistance Plan becomes available (CRS; a university financial aid office page describes the same changes).
The government moves to dismiss the multistate challenge or, alternatively, for summary judgment; briefing in the first case ends in early November 2026.

title: Cap federal student borrowing, end PLUS loans, and replace income-driven repayment
uncertainties: The statute text was not read directly (govinfo's HTML and PDF of Public Law 119-21 stop partway through the first title when fetched, and congress.gov blocks automated fetching); loan limits, Parent PLUS limits, the Repayment Assistance Plan formula and the phase-out dates come from the CRS report (R48727, first issued 2025-09-29 and updated 2026-01-08) as read through a fetch summary, whose last 27,000 characters were not read. The CRS text gives no separate SAVE or PAYE end dates; ED's 2026-07-08 notice (per an earlier Federal Register listing) says PAYE and ICR sunset in 2028. The final rule's preamble was read only to its first 100,000 of about 135,000 characters. Not checked: the SAVE plan's status, how many borrowers moved to the new plan, and whether ED has taken further steps on professional-degree rulemaking after the 2026-06-24 ruling. The litigation facts rest on one law-firm summary (Thompson Coburn, 2026-09-30); court opinions were not read. Refutation check 2026-10-28: a University of Washington federal relations post (2026-06-25) calls the 2026-06-24 D.D.C. order a preliminary injunction and says the new caps deadline is blocked for affected programs, while the Thompson Coburn summary says set aside and stayed; neither source was a court opinion, and the exact reach of the order for borrowers in affected programs was not confirmed. The order was described as limited to the professional-degree definition. Statutory caps, Grad PLUS end and RAP were reported as taking effect 2026-07-01. In review on 2026-10-28 the court status was changed from upheld to pending: the 2026-09-25 entry is a government motion, not a ruling, and the Thompson Coburn summary reports no decision upholding the rule.
